editorial:
Imagine a strict Catholic French couple who thought they had everything figured out, until their four daughters each fall for men from completely different backgrounds. That is the heart of this comedy, and it plays out like a big, loud family dinner where nobody agrees on anything. The parents are shocked, confused, and constantly trying to keep their old traditions alive while their daughters happily ignore them. It is funny, warm, and full of awkward moments that feel real.

The acting is strong, especially the parents who carry the movie with perfect comic timing. The pacing keeps things moving, though some jokes repeat a bit too often. If you enjoy culture-clash humor and family chaos, you will have a great time. It is best enjoyed with friends or family. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the parents finally accept their sons-in-law after a big family gathering goes wrong in a funny way. The twist is that the youngest daughter announces she is marrying a man from yet another background, sending the parents right back into panic. The movie ends with the family laughing together, showing that love wins over old habits, even if the parents never fully stop complaining.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family comedies and culture-clash humor.
